questions.question: In value-based pricing, what determines your price?
questions.questionHtml: In value-based pricing, what determines your price?

answers.text: The value your service delivers to the customer
answers.textHtml: The value your service delivers to the customer

answers.text: The minimum wage in your area

questions.feedback: Value-based pricing sets your price based on how much value you deliver to the customer, not your costs or competitors' prices.
questions.feedbackHtml: Value-based pricing sets your price based on how much value you deliver to the customer.

questions.question: What does the fast-cheap-good triangle tell us?
questions.questionHtml: What does the fast-cheap-good triangle tell us?

answers.text: Customers can have all three if they pay enough
answers.textHtml: Customers can have all three if they pay enough

answers.text: Customers can only pick two of the three
answers.textHtml: Customers can only pick two of the three

answers.text: Fast service is always the most important
answers.textHtml: Fast service is always the most important

answers.text: Cheap services are always low quality

questions.feedback: The fast-cheap-good triangle shows that customers can only choose two: good and fast is not cheap, good and cheap is not fast, and fast and cheap is not good.
questions.feedbackHtml: Customers can only choose two of the three attributes at once.

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: Which are common pricing mistakes to avoid?
questions.questionHtml: Select ALL that apply: Which are common pricing mistakes to avoid?

answers.text: Being the lowest-priced option in the market
answers.textHtml: Being the lowest-priced option in the market

answers.text: Using psychological pricing like $995 instead of $1000
Forgetting to account for travel time and expenses
answers.textHtml: Forgetting to account for travel time and expenses

questions.feedback: Being the cheapest signals low quality. Underestimating costs and forgetting travel expenses destroy profitability. Psychological pricing is a valid strategy, not a mistake.
questions.feedbackHtml: Being cheapest, underestimating costs, and forgetting travel expenses are common pricing mistakes. Psychological pricing is a valid strategy.

questions.question: Why should you always show the full price on invoices even when giving a discount?
questions.questionHtml: Why should you always show the full price on invoices even when giving a discount?

answers.text: So the client understands the true value and does not expect the discount permanently
answers.textHtml: So the client understands the true value and does not expect the discount permanently

answers.text: To make the invoice look more professional
answers.textHtml: To make the invoice look more professional

questions.feedback: Showing the full price ensures the client understands the real value of your service and will not expect the discounted price to be your standard rate.
questions.feedbackHtml: Showing full value ensures clients understand the discount is a gesture, not your standard pricing.

questions.question: Match each pricing method to its approach:
questions.questionHtml: Match each pricing method to its approach:

answers.matchText: Price relative to what competitors charge
Price based on the benefit delivered to the client
answers.matchTextHtml: Price based on the benefit delivered to the client

answers.matchText: Calculate all costs then add a markup percentage
answers.matchTextHtml: Calculate all costs then add a markup percentage

questions.feedback: Market-based pricing uses competitor rates, value-based uses customer benefit, and cost-plus adds a markup to your total costs.
questions.feedbackHtml: Each method uses a different basis: competitors, customer value, or your own costs.
